evidence.summary: Generation and SHA bytes scale with history size, while the sampled commit remains about 14.6-20.8 ms through 500 records and 21 filesystem barriers in the isolated probe.
All publication failpoints recover to the old generation or the complete new batch; no partial batch is visible.

metadata.residual: full-generation rewrite/hash is asymptotically linear but not dominant in the 500-record probe

reproduction.instructions: Run Store history scaling at 1, 10, 50, 100, 250, and 500 records, record generation and SHA bytes plus fsync count and commit latency, then fault-inject every atomic batch publication boundary and verify recovery exposes only the old or complete new generation.

summary: The Store now provides generic generation-bound lookup maps and atomic multi-object publication, and Forge uses the latter to publish a receipt plus terminal verifier result in one generation. Isolated generation measurements remain approximately linear in total history bytes: 148 bytes at one record, 1,264 at ten, 6,224 at fifty, 12,424 at one hundred, 31,024 at 250, and 62,024 at 500; the sampled commit remained filesystem-barrier dominated at about 14.6-20.8 ms. The residual is representation write amplification and the separate portable-WASM resource envelope, not a cross-backend value disagreement.

workaround.description: Use the admitted research-bytecode backend for the effectful Store application and the generic Store batch boundary; preserve the larger portable-WASM fuel envelope for composite/table workloads.
